Releasing RdistNN 0.1.0

Source: RELEASING.md

The initial public release introduces CATE and nonparametric regression with DNN weights, jackknife uncertainty, tuning, diagnostics, and plots. PLQR and local IV-GMM remain experimental. Publishing this release does not promote those interfaces to stable status.

Prepare and verify the final source

Run from the repository root with package dependencies and development tools installed as described in CONTRIBUTING.md.

  1. Confirm that DESCRIPTION, NEWS.md, and the intended tag agree on version 0.1.0. Regenerate help and README from their sources:

    devtools::document()
devtools::build_readme()

  2. Run the alignment checks in CONTRIBUTING.md, then build the installable source package with all vignettes and check that exact archive:

    dir.create("archives", showWarnings = FALSE)
src <- devtools::build(path = "archives", vignettes = TRUE, manual = FALSE)
rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(
  src, args = "--no-manual", error_on = "warning",
  check_dir = "archives/check"
)

    Investigate all errors and warnings, and review any notes. Inspect the archive’s file list: it should contain package code, generated help, tests, and built vignettes, while excluding private notes, agent settings, CI logs, prior archives, and repository-only publication instructions. archives/ is ignored and excluded from future source builds.

  3. Build the documentation site, including examples and articles:

    pkgdown::build_site()

    Review docs/index.html, docs/articles/getting-started.html, and docs/reference/index.html. Verify that CATE and regression lead the onboarding and that PLQR topics are grouped and labeled experimental. The generated docs/ directory is ignored. The canonical site URL is https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/.

  4. Review the final diff. Require passing R-CMD-check on Linux, Windows, macOS arm64, and macOS x86-64 for the release commit, plus the alignment checks. CI also covers R release, devel, and oldrel on Linux. Local checks do not substitute for this platform matrix. Reuse successful validation while the source snapshot is unchanged.

Publish on GitHub

Create the v0.1.0 tag and GitHub release from the verified commit. Use the release-scope section of NEWS.md for the introduction, followed by a link to the getting-started guide and the explicit PLQR experimental status.

Attach RdistNN_0.1.0.tar.gz, built above, as the installable R source asset. GitHub’s automatically generated repository ZIP/tarball and the CI source-snapshot ZIP are repository snapshots; the R source package includes built vignettes and applies .Rbuildignore exclusions. Include a checksum:

cd archives
sha256sum RdistNN_0.1.0.tar.gz > SHA256SUMS

After publication, download both assets without credentials and run sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS from their download directory. Install the downloaded tarball in a fresh library and execute the getting-started examples. For version-pinned GitHub installation, use pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN@v0.1.0"); the default branch remains available for development installations.

Users can install a downloaded source asset with:

install.packages("Rcpp")  # required dependency, if not already installed
install.packages("RdistNN_0.1.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

Source installation needs C++17. Optional visualization requires ggplot2 (and patchwork for dashboards); other suggested dependencies support development, replication, or experimental workflows.

Publishing a GitHub release triggers .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml, which builds the site and deploys it to gh-pages. Confirm that this workflow succeeds and GitHub Pages serves that branch before announcing the public documentation links. A manual run of the same workflow can refresh the site without a release. Neither local site building nor pushing package sources alone deploys the site.

Introduce the package on jakobjuergens.com

WEBSITE.md contains a short software entry and release announcement ready to copy into the website’s existing format. Link to the GitHub release and canonical documentation site after both are live. Keep the package documentation on its canonical URL rather than duplicating its reference pages on the personal site. Review both links after publication.

This file records publication steps; preparing files or building the local site does not itself tag, publish, or deploy a release.
